page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-2 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the n1 server family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon core operating at 2.3 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding 0.9 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations place this server in the lower performance tiers. The stress-ng single-core metric is 1086.39, while the multi-core score reaches 1408.88. Memory bandwidth is limited, with large-block read and write speeds recorded at 13.22 GB/sec and 11.3 GB/sec respectively. Cryptographic and compression tasks also reflect these hardware constraints, with a Passmark CPU score of 1638.85 and a static web serving throughput of 1.51 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-highcpu-2 offers a low-cost entry point for compute-focused workloads that do not require substantial memory capacity. However, the low RAM-to-vCPU ratio represents a significant tradeoff for memory-intensive applications. This server is best suited for lightweight compute tasks, basic web serving, small-scale Redis operations, or simple utility scripts that fit within the 2.0 GB memory envelope.
